title: Embedding credit velocity and enterprise QSA checklist
creator: Asha Patel
description: Run a cohort-based pricing experiment that tests per-vector credit velocity discounts (time-bound acceleration credits) for enterprise customers while capturing required security questionnaire (QSA) updates and contract guardrails.
background: Customers building large reranking pipelines reported that bursty ingestion patterns make per-vector economics unpredictable. Sales requests two levers: (1) a short-lived credit velocity mechanism to smooth billing spikes for committed customers, and (2) clearer contract language & QSA evidence that maps to the new construct. Previous experiments focused on long-term batch discounts and slab pricing; this ticket explores a complementary short-duration mechanism that preserves unit economics.
proposal_summary: Introduce a 30-day ‘velocity credit’ bucket for committed enterprise customers that grants temporary per-vector discounts triggered by commit thresholds. Run this as a controlled experiment with 3 cohorts (control, standard velocity, enhanced velocity). Parallel work: update QSA artifacts (dataflow diagrams, encryption evidence, RBAC config) and add contract annex language describing the velocity mechanism and audit windows.
experiment_design: Cohorts: (A) Control - existing per-vector pricing, (B) Velocity Tier 1 - 20% per-vector discount for first 2M vectors/day for 30 days after activation, (C) Velocity Tier 2 - 35% discount for first 4M vectors/day for 30 days.

Eligibility: enterprise customers with active committed spend >= $50k/month or Dedicated customers with Reserved capacity contracts. Enrollment via Sales order or self-serve toggle in Console (pilot-only).

Activation: customers can opt-in to trigger their velocity bucket; Sales may also enable for trial cohorts. Velocity credits are single-use 30-day windows with cooldown of 60 days between activations.
Billing: discounts applied at invoice-level as billing credits tied to per-vector units consumed during the 30-day window. Backend flags track activation_id and start/end timestamps for auditability.

Observability: add dashboard with cohort breakdown, vectors/day, discounted vectors, effective CPM, and revenue delta projected over 12 months. Capture token-level logs for sampling and cost reconciliation.
Duration: 90-day experiment with phased enrollments to limit operational blast radius.
success_metrics: Primary: Maintain or improve gross margin on cohort-adjusted usage (target: margin delta <= -2% vs control).
Primary: Increase net retention for participating customers by >= 4 percentage points at 90 days post-activation.
Secondary: Reduce customer support & contract negotiation cycles for burst pricing questions by 40% (measured via ticket tags).
Secondary: 30% of eligible enrollments opt to reactivate velocity window after cooldown (signal of perceived value).
rollout_plan: Week 0-2: Finalize experiment parameters, contract language draft, and QSA checklist items. Build feature flag and billing credit pipeline.
Week 3-5: Implement and QA backend billing logic; add cohort telemetry and Console UI hooks for Sales toggles. Prepare dashboards and reconciliation jobs.
Week 6: Run a 1-week internal pilot with 2 friendly customers to validate flows and billing calculations.
Week 7-12: Open pilot to 10 enterprise customers across industry verticals. Collect qualitative feedback from Customer Success and Sales.
Week 13: Analyze results, make margin adjustments or cadence changes, and propose product decision (ga/iterate/rollback).
qsa_tasks: Update dataflow diagrams to include velocity activation metadata stored in billing database and audit logs.
Produce evidence for encryption-at-rest/in-transit for billing artifacts (S3 storage, RDS snapshots).
Document RBAC controls for who can activate velocity windows (Sales role vs. Customer Admin).
Add retention policy and deletion flow for activation records to QSA artifact bundle.
Prepare answers for common Qs: auditability, reconciliation proof, SLA impact, and data residency implications.
contract_changes: Annex: "Velocity Credit" definition, scope, activation mechanism, and limitations (single-use window, cooldown, termination for abuse).
Billing Addendum: how credits appear on invoices and sample invoice line-items for velocity discounts.
Audit Clause: rights to inspect activation logs for customers with compliance requirements; sample notice windows for audits.
Termination/Abuse Policy: clear guardrails if customers attempt to game velocity windows across accounts.
acceptance_criteria: Feature flag exists to enable velocity cohorts and activation flows in Console and Sales tools.
Billing credits are calculated correctly for sampled invoices (reconciliation variance <= 0.5%).
QSA artifact bundle updated and reviewed by Security (attestation email thread in comments).
Contract annex template drafted and reviewed by Legal and Sales Ops.
Telemetry dashboard shows per-cohort metrics and the experiment pipeline emits activation events for every activation.
notes: We aim for a pricing primitive that complements existing batch/commit discounts without creating a long-lived revenue hole. Legal emphasized clear audit windows. Security requested explicit retention and encryption evidence for billing activations.
